Prevention: Purchase certified crop seed and animal feed to reduce the chance of contamination
As seeds can travel on animals and machinery, do not allow animals into an affected area, limit machinery use in the area and keep machinery clean to prevent spread
Keep crop healthy to maximize competitiveness - use optimal water and fertilizer levels
Limit the amount the tillage where
Post-harvest tillage may promote survival since seeds become buried
Do not allow livestock to graze on sparse pasture where weed is present.
Livestock otherwise may eat the poisonous weed.
Monitoring: Seedling leaves: oval-shaped, pointed tips, few or no lobes
Mature leaves: oval to broadly triangular-shaped, unevenly toothed
Flowers: trumpet-shaped, white to creamy or violet, rarely completely open
Seed capsules/cases: egg-shaped, walnut-sized, spiny or bald
May be confused with other species within the
D. stramonium : 100 or more capsule spines; long flower (up to 10 cm)
D. ferox : up to 60 capsule spines; shorter flower (4-6 cm)
D. ferox ): straight capsule stalks; black or grey seeds.
D. leichhardtii , D. metel , D. inoxia and
D. wrightii : curved capsule stalks; brown or yellow seeds
Monitor open and disturbed areas particularly closely.
D. stramonium can be found on roadsides, agricultural land and riverbanks.
Take action as soon as weed is seen
Direct Control: Dig, pull or hoe out before seed sets in order to prevent it spreading.
Wear gloves when handling it since it is poisonous, particularly its leaves and seeds.
Be thorough since it can regenerate from root fragments if not removed effectively
To dispose of pulled weed, if seed has not set, add to a compost heap.
If seed has set, ensure pulled weed is buried to least 60 cm/2 ft, or burn it to prevent spread (if permitted in your country)
Till the soil when weeds are seedlings.
When mature, stems become woody and difficult to remove
Grow winter annual crops and forage crops and cut them several times during the year to control the weed
Remove weed before making hay, silage, grain or other animal feed to prevent spread
Seedlings emerge over a long period of time so repeated removal may be necessary
